subject: The campaign target sits 16% above llama.cpp's own result on the same artifact; the two pending decisions land at 92.6% of llama.cpp
findings: The campaign's target of 80.2 tok/s is 16.4% above llama.cpp's 68.92 on the same artifact and hardware, so it requires beating the reference implementation, not merely matching it.

The comparison basis is not like-for-like: the target is 70% of Qwen3.6-35B-A3B's 114.57, a different model with fewer active parameters (A3B vs A4B). The same-artifact llama.cpp figure is the reference that isolates engine quality.

The two pending lead decisions - accepting the decode attention split (+5.3%, measured) and authoring a selected GEMV that reaches the MoE's 0.94 ms roofline - land at 63.79 tok/s, 92.6% of llama.cpp. That is the reachable envelope from the work already identified.
The 63.79 figure is an upper bound on that path: it assumes the MoE kernel reaches its roofline, and that kernel does not exist yet. The split half of it is measured.
Reaching 80.2 would additionally require beating llama.cpp on attention and the dense projections, on top of both decisions above.
recommendation: Re-base the campaign's target on the same-artifact llama.cpp reference (68.92 tok/s), where 92.6% is a near-term, measurable goal from work already identified, rather than on 70% of a different model's throughput. Presented as arithmetic for the lead to decide, not taken.
